title: LLD interview framework & UML basics
relevance: High - the pacing/structure for every LLD / OOD / machine-coding round (campus + experienced); Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, PhonePe, Atlassian, Amazon, Google, Meta all grade how you go requirements -> entities -> class diagram -> patterns -> code, not pattern name-dropping alone.
company_notes: Common in India product company machine-coding rounds (Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, PhonePe, Cred) as clarify -> design -> code -> demo, and in big-tech LLD/OOD rounds (Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft) as discussion + class structure + extensibility. This framework is foundational across recurring prompts like parking lot, Splitwise, elevator, Stack Overflow, games, and booking systems.

phases.goal: Establish scope and a repeatable interview flow before any class design.

must_hit.point: Begins with requirements: functional operations, actors, rules/state transitions, errors, and explicit out-of-scope boundaries (UI, DB, network).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They ask clarifying questions first and explicitly state what is excluded.

must_hit.point: Writes 4-8 requirement bullets and marks MUST vs NICE before proposing entities.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They produce a short scoped list and get confirmation before moving on.

must_hit.point: States and follows the pipeline requirements -> entities -> class diagram -> patterns -> walkthrough, announcing phase transitions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They narrate where they are in the loop so interviewer pacing stays aligned.

probes: Before you draw classes, what are your must-have operations and what is out of scope?
Can you outline your step-by-step flow for this LLD round?

hints.1: Start by clarifying what the system must do, not which pattern to use.
hints.2: List actors, operations, state rules, failure cases, and explicit exclusions, then separate MUST from NICE.
hints.3: Use the standard flow: requirements, entities, class APIs/relationships, then patterns, then walkthrough.

phases.goal: Translate scoped requirements into a coherent class model and interview-appropriate UML.

must_hit.point: Uses noun/verb extraction: nouns become candidate classes, verbs become methods; keeps ~4-7 core entities plus one orchestrator/Facade.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They filter out mere attributes as fields/enums and keep one coordinator class like ParkingLot/Game/StackOverflow.

must_hit.point: Defines each class as state + behavior tied to use cases, with rules owned by the state holder (encapsulation/tell-don't-ask).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Methods enforce domain rules inside owning objects instead of dumping logic externally.

must_hit.point: Uses UML basics correctly: class compartments, visibility (+ - # ~), relationship meanings, and multiplicity (1, 0..1, *, 1..*).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Their arrows/labels distinguish association, aggregation, composition, inheritance/generalization, realization, and dependency.

probes: From this requirement text, which nouns become classes and which stay as fields/enums?
Show one relationship where composition is correct and one where aggregation is correct.

hints.1: Map verbs to APIs and keep only nouns with real state/rules as classes.
hints.2: For each class, list fields that enforce constraints and methods that map to use cases.
hints.3: Pick one orchestrator, then connect entities with clear relationship and multiplicity choices.

phases.goal: Demonstrate judgment on notation depth, pattern usage, and round-style constraints.

must_hit.point: Treats formal UML as optional by default and asks interviewer preference (boxes/arrows vs strict notation).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They prioritize clarity and switch notation depth if requested.

must_hit.point: Applies patterns after class design, choosing 0-2 patterns only when variation exists.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They describe the design problem first, then justify Strategy/Factory/Observer/State/Facade only if needed.

must_hit.point: Adapts approach to round type: OOD is discussion + diagram/stubs, while machine coding prioritizes working must-haves with design <=15-20% time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They explicitly rebalance depth vs coding speed based on interview format.

probes: Why are you using this pattern here, and what would happen if you skipped it?
If I asked for formal UML now, how would your representation change?

hints.1: Do not optimize for notation or pattern count before solving the stated problem.
hints.2: First identify what varies; then decide whether a pattern buys extensibility.
hints.3: For machine coding, cap design time and deliver mandatory behavior before optional abstractions.

phases.goal: Prove the design works end-to-end through concrete execution and edge-case reasoning.

must_hit.point: Closes with a collaboration trace: one happy path and 2-3 edge cases.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They can narrate object interactions for scenarios like self-vote, full lot, or invalid move.

must_hit.point: In machine coding, implements models -> services -> Main and demonstrates must-have behavior before nice-to-have additions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Demo works for core use cases and optional features are explicitly deferred.

must_hit.point: Maintains interview pacing checkpoints (e.g., 45-60 min OOD or 90 min machine coding) without skipping requirements lock-in.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They time-box phases and still preserve clarify -> design -> code -> walkthrough order.

probes: Walk me through one end-to-end use case and then an edge case that breaks naive designs.
If you had 10 more minutes, what would you add after mandatory features?

hints.1: Show how objects collaborate on a concrete request, not just class lists.
hints.2: Trace call flow step-by-step and include one failure/constraint path.
hints.3: Run a happy path first, then edge paths, and state the next incremental extension.

tradeoffs.topic: Formal UML notation vs communication speed
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Communication quality is prioritized over strict UML ceremony; simplified boxes/arrows are acceptable unless interviewer asks for formal diamonds/arrows and multiplicities.
Patterns are chosen after requirements/entities/APIs are clear; 1-2 justified patterns are stronger than naming many patterns without an actual variation point.

tradeoffs.topic: Design depth vs implementation completeness (machine coding)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Time-box design to <=15-20% and ship mandatory behavior first; extensibility and extras come after a working demo.
An orchestrator coordinates flow, but rule enforcement belongs inside state-owning domain objects to avoid both god classes and anemic models.

gotchas.trap: Jumping to code before locking requirements and scope.
gotchas.correction: Start with clarifications, write scoped bullets, and confirm must-haves/out-of-scope first.

gotchas.trap: Pattern name-dropping or forcing Singleton/Factory everywhere.
gotchas.correction: Introduce patterns only after class sketch and only for a clear variation point.

gotchas.trap: Over-indexing on full UML or skipping UML expectations entirely.
gotchas.correction: Ask what notation the interviewer wants, then use the simplest representation that communicates design clearly.

gotchas.trap: God Manager class handling all business logic.
gotchas.correction: Keep orchestrator for coordination and push domain rules into the objects that own state.

gotchas.trap: Anemic models with getters only where behavior belongs in entities.
gotchas.correction: Attach behavior to data owners so invariants are enforced through methods, not external scripts.

gotchas.trap: Ignoring mandatory vs optional features in machine coding.
gotchas.correction: Deliver a working must-have demo first, then explicitly call out optional next steps.
Finish with a happy-path walkthrough plus edge cases (or a short sequence-style trace) to validate object interaction.
